reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes participation in a token-based mining scheme by claiming that submitted tokens will generate OneCoins and that the token amount will double after a split. It gives step-by-step instructions to submit tokens immediately, uses urgency about avoiding a higher per-coin rate, and tells viewers to pass the video to team members. The video actively encourages participation in a mining-for-income mechanism rather than merely discussing or criticizing it.

Immediately after the split, the number will double.
Make sure you do this immediately after any split that you have tokens waiting.
you want to put that number here in the tokens to submit, and click submit
video on so that your team members know

opening.argument: The presentation does not state that submitting tokens guarantees a financial return or that viewers will receive a particular amount of OneCoins. It explains a claimed timing difference around a split and a reevaluation, using conditional language such as “may see” when describing what the interface displays. The dashboard also presents multiple account categories rather than establishing that any displayed figure is cash or a guaranteed payout. On this record, the material can be read as practical information about how the platform represents mining activity, not a promise that participation will produce income.

citations.quote: you may see this either change from you are not mining to you are mining
The reason why it is important to submit the tokens immediately is that onecoin will re-evaluate a new value placed on onecoin with the difficulty rate

rebuttal.rebuttal: The instructions show how the platform is operated, but they do not establish that the speaker guarantees profits, certifies the system, or promises a particular outcome. “Start mining OneCoins” describes the stated platform function; it does not by itself prove that the video represents mining as a reliable income source. The dashboard likewise displays account fields without proving those figures can be withdrawn or realized.

citations.quote: so they can start mining OneCoins for you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The conditional phrase “may see” qualifies only the interface update, not the underlying promotion. The video still tells viewers to submit tokens so the system can mine OneCoins for them, gives an immediate-action rationale, and describes a higher rate per coin after reevaluation. Those are operational claims about obtaining coins, not merely neutral risk discussion. The dashboard’s account labels do not remove the token-submission mechanism.

opening.argument: The clearest characterization is an operational walkthrough of a website workflow. The title identifies a how-to subject, and the narration walks through locating the mining area, entering an available-token amount, submitting it, and checking the dashboard for a status change. The sampled interface visibly contains mining controls, token fields, capacity information, and transaction information, consistent with a software demonstration. Showing viewers where controls are and explaining possible interface updates is educational instruction about using a platform; it does not independently establish that the creator is soliciting an investment or guaranteeing returns.

The narration explains navigation and system behavior, while the frames show a software interface. “Pass this video on” can equally mean sharing operational instructions with users who already have access, not recruiting purchasers.
